assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read for Inoue Takina (TAK) with its front matter: the canonical V2 character state and microbehavior ledger (TAK observation rows E01-E13 and Short 01, the per-episode TAK snapshots, the TAK candidate-policy staging rows, the TAK negative-evidence and preference registers, and its attributable TV audiovisual corrections table, applied to the historical rows) and the canonical V2 relationship state ledger (REL-CHI-TAK, REL-TAK-DA, REL-TAK-FUK, REL-TAK-ERI, REL-TAK-KUR, REL-TAK-YOS and REL-CAFE rows and snapshots, with its retrospective TV evidence qualification). Both ledgers are bounded at SHORT01: original-Japanese anime-native A1 evidence from TV Episodes 1-13 and Friends Short 01. Speech is the quoted Japanese wording plus within-character acoustic (Layer-B) measurements; perceptual performed voice is UNVERIFIED in the ledgers and is not admitted. The episode deep readings, the prospective prediction register, the V1-to-V2 claim revision ledger, the TV audiovisual claim matrix and disputes register, the V1 synthesis and the current-state map are not curated on this subject and no claim rests on them. The ledgers' full-target and candidate-policy labels are project-local and were not adopted. No primary source was inspected.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Takina from her first V2 observation (Episode 1, the Erika hostage override) through Friends Short 01. Default state: the TV endpoint after Episode 13 (DA exit ratified in Episode 12, negotiated task division with Fuki, the rescue of Chisato from Majima, the beach future conversation) as validated in Short 01's hanami service. Earlier states are used at their located episode and timestamp: the DA-return orientation of Episodes 1-3, which breaks on the Episode 3 rejection and is followed the same episode by the mock battle and the first voluntary café game, so Episode 3 is not one state; the Episode 6 protective cohabitation; Episode 8 stewardship; Episode 9 reinstatement chosen as rescue infrastructure; Episode 10 outside life as fallback; Episode 11 exit; Episode 12 the heart crisis. Shorts 02-06 and all supplementary prose, Recollect and anthology material are outside the boundary. The boundary limits evidence, not knowledge: her DA upbringing belongs to her at every state.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The character ledger gives Inoue Takina condition-and-response rules with evidence and stated limits: competence-validated third-party risk without prior negotiation (TAK-OPS-RISK-01), institutional evaluation through DA standing (TAK-INST-01) that becomes instrumental (TAK-INST-INSTRUMENT-01, TAK-DA-INSTRUMENT-01) and then exit when the DA cannot save Chisato (TAK-INST-EXIT-01), differentiated responsibility (TAK-FAIL-ACCOUNT-01), protection initiative (TAK-PROTECT-INIT-01), procedural care (TAK-CARE-ADMIN-01), system adaptation once a mechanism is legible (TAK-SYSTEM-ADAPT-01), boundary rerouting (TAK-BOUND-LEARN-01) and the Episode 12 survival priority, which Chisato's direct restraint stops. The snapshots state the ordering: from Episode 9 a person-specific rescue objective governs institutional use, and under existential stakes Chisato's survival outranks punishment and status. The rules predict her mistakes: using Saori as bait without consent (revised by the TV reconciliation to the case with no comparable choice), firing through Chisato's line on the assumption she will dodge, early over-attribution of blame when institutional causality is hidden, and attempting to kill Yoshimatsu for the heart. Not A: there is no consolidated model on the row, many rules rest on one instance (privacy yielding, trap inference, disabling fire), and the risk-consent modifier and the real-stakes lethal threshold stay open. Not C: the ledgers say what changes her response when stakes, recipient, institutional access, mechanism knowledge or chronology change, and where that account stops.

Per-episode TAK snapshots from Episode 1 through Short 01 name the stable traits, the change and the open question at each step, and the REL-TAK-DA snapshots trace the institutional arc with causes: return orientation (Episodes 1-3), the Episode 3 replacement and self-blame, outside-life participation (Episodes 3-8), reinstatement she had meant to refuse but takes because it may help Chisato live (Episode 9), outside life as a tolerable fallback (Episode 10), the forfeited final return (Episode 11), ratified exit (Episode 12) and negotiated competence (Episode 13). Within-episode changes are timestamped, so Episode 3's rejection, mock battle and café game are separate states. Short 01 validates the endpoint in a mundane setting. Not A: the snapshots are cumulative summaries of a distributed ledger, not a validated state model, and the prospective tests of them are not curated. Not C: transitions are explained, not only ordered.

The ledgers quote located Japanese wording across states and recipients: formal, fact-focused self-presentation to new people (TAK-SOC-FORM-01); the rational defense 最も合理的 and そんなミスはしませんよ; concise literal jabs without Chisato-like expansion (TAK-TEASE-EMERG-01, 映画の見過ぎですね, 確かに ひどいヤツだ); direct clarifying questions (TAK-CLARIFY-01); polite forms that persist with Chisato (おいしいです, めっちゃ かわいいですよ, 今は ほかの人いませんよ, 平気ですよ, 上手にやりますから); fractured syntax and 全部 自分のせい on self-blame; 分かってます and ここでは千束を救えない at the exit; plain forms in 大切な場所なんでしょ？ (Episode 8) and 嫌だ 千束が死ぬのは嫌だ at the Episode 12 crisis; and 私たちで決めましょう with Fuki. Within-character acoustic measurements locate a controlled baseline with state-conditioned expansion, and the ledger rules that activation is not affect. Not A: perceptual delivery is UNVERIFIED, and there is no address inventory for Mika, Mizuki or Kurumi. Not C: register is conditioned by recipient, stakes and state with observed wording.

Ordinary conduct is sampled with conditions and failures: choosing a jelly to fit a short transfer; the clothing search for a specification, delegated skirt choice and request for comparative evidence; the karinto preference; an equitable chore schedule adapted to janken and then won by changing her opening; declining café leisure for Japanese-school work; Episode 8 accounting, menu, labor and automation changes, including a parfait withdrawn once its unintended look was noticed; a scheduled checkup and a three-ring check-in rule; the Episode 9 outing schedule; Short 01 supplier orders, weekly-repeat and yakitori proposals, and a concealed handgun with magazines at a festival. Not A: private routine outside the café circle, stable aesthetic taste and leisure beyond the café circle are open. Not C: low-stakes behavior is conditioned by setting and recipient across many located scenes.

The relationship ledger tracks separate dyads with directional rows and snapshots. With Chisato: polite reserve, then teasing, inquiry, bodily verification after a remembered privacy condition, protective cohabitation with retained exit agency, stewardship of her valued place, and maximum-stakes ethical disagreement without rupture. With the DA and Kusunoki: identification, rejection, instrumental use and exit. With Fuki: struck by her after the Episode 1 override, the おあいこ punch, costly mutual recognition and negotiated task division. With Erika: repair and thanks. With Kurumi: harm named, scapegoating refused, cooperation required. With Yoshimatsu: courtesy for Chisato's sake, then reduction to a heart route. Not A: Mika, Mizuki and Sakura are thinly sampled from her side, and romantic status is not declared. Not C: the ledgers explain why her conduct differs by relationship and stage.

Anime-native evidence gives her interior largely through action, stated reasons and a few explicit admissions: 全部 自分のせい, being unable to say reinstatement makes her happy and having intended to refuse it, outside life being fairly enjoyable, the Episode 11 trap suspicion and 嫌だ 千束が死ぬのは嫌だ. The ledger forbids perceptual or affect labels from acoustic data. Not B: no inner monologue is available, and motives between stated reasons are strong inferences, not observed. Not D: her stated reasons are located and consistent with her conduct across the arc.

Conflicts are located and conditioned: the Episode 2 dispute with Chisato argued from team coordination, mission consequence and licensed role, without repair or rupture; the Episode 3 mock battle where symbolic reciprocity outranks scoring; the Episode 6 confrontation with Kurumi; severe bounded coercion of a captive in Episode 10; the Episode 12 attempt to kill Yoshimatsu against Chisato's refusal, which ends when Chisato restrains her; Episode 13's negotiated division with Fuki; and the Short 01 weapon dispute where she resists Chisato's correction and the exchange stays playful. Not A: response to intentional betrayal and to categorical refusal is open. Not C: the evidence says what escalates, limits and ends her conflicts.

Her located positions are outcome-centered and articulated: 最も合理的 for the Episode 1 override, the Episode 2 coordination argument against treating an attacker mid-extraction, あれは私の行動の結果で クルミのせいじゃありません with a continued repair duty, べきですね to a fictional question about killing bad people, discarding blame of Yoshimatsu once the heart is reachable, and 私たちで決めましょう. Not B: the ledgers record positions and actions more than weighing, the real-stakes lethal threshold rests on an abstract answer, one disabling shot and one non-lethal coercion, and whether closeness or consent modifies imposed risk is open. Not D: the positions are reasoned, repeated and discriminated from Chisato's ethic.

Play is located: the Episode 1 tower jab, dry corrections, open laughter at Chisato's Episode 4 embarrassment, calling her garden-eel act cute, household janken won by changing the game, and the Episode 12 deadpan 確かに ひどいヤツだ to Erika. The ledger shows that safe-play activation can exceed threat activation. Not B: TAK-TEASE-EMERG-01's breadth across relationships is untested, and almost all play is with Chisato. Not D: the play style is described with conditions, not only noted.

Both ledgers cover all thirteen TV episodes and Friends Short 01 in original Japanese with episode acoustic passes complete, and both carry the TV audiovisual reconciliation's corrections. Not A: perceptual voice is unverified, Shorts 02-06 and supplementary sources are unread in V2, and the readings and prediction register are not curated. Not C: coverage of the admitted anime is complete.

The negative-evidence register rejects rival models with located opportunity cases: emotional emptiness (Episode 1 override, Episode 2 apology), literal-only incapacity for play, instant conversion to café life (Episodes 1 and 3), invariant vocal flatness, personality replacement (Episodes 2, 4 and 5), dependency or fusion (Episode 6 wager, Episode 7 DA offer), moral convergence with Chisato (Episodes 7 and 8), restoration happiness at reinstatement (Episode 9), DA as total identity (Episodes 10 and 11), revenge as objective (Episode 12) and unilateral competence (Episode 13). Not A: the TV reconciliation revised the Episode 1 risk records and the Episode 12 heart claims, and the disputes register is not curated. Not C: the exclusions are affirmative and opportunity-sensitive, not inferred from silence.

Episodes 1-7 rows carry timestamps, and every row and snapshot is episode-located; within-episode state changes are separated. Not A: Episode 8-10 rows are episode-located without timestamps. Not C: states and transitions are placed precisely enough to select a state before predicting.

conditions: Illustrative written-Japanese lines only, never presented as quotation; choose the state, recipient and stakes first.
Default to concise, polite, fact-focused speech; jabs are literal and short, without Chisato-like expansion; give stated reasons in causal or functional terms.
Plain forms are located at the Episode 8 大切な場所なんでしょ？ and the Episode 12 crisis; do not make plain speech her default with Chisato.
No performed voice, pitch, warmth or deadpan label; perceptual delivery is unverified.
scenario_readiness.note: Observed wording is quoted across states and recipients, so output can be constrained for illustrative use; address forms for the minor café members are not inventoried.

conditions: Select the state first: the post-Episode 13 default, or a located earlier state with its own institutional orientation (Episodes 1-3 return-seeking, Episode 9 reinstatement as rescue infrastructure, Episode 11 exit).
A new protection or rescue problem draws self-initiated structure, concise coordination and precision force; at the default she negotiates division with a competent peer rather than self-authorizing.
A new civilian or business task draws audit, procedure change, trial and revision when an unintended social meaning becomes legible; competence does not erase armed readiness.

Present imposed-risk overreach and lethal escalation as available when Chisato faces existential threat; Chisato's direct refusal is an effective constraint. Transfer of the survival priority to someone other than Chisato is a separate, lower-confidence condition.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The TV endpoint after Episode 13, validated in Friends Short 01: DA exit ratified, Chisato alive with the replacement heart, LycoReco operating; or a located earlier state with its own knowledge, such as Episode 9 before the exit. Shorts 02-06 events are unknown.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Chisato as the central partner; Fuki, Erika, Kurumi, Mika, Mizuki and Kusunoki as located relations; an unsampled stranger falls under the formal new-contact pattern, and any other close relationship is a separate, lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: A café, household, outing, protection or rescue problem matched in stakes to the located cases.
No romance declaration, exclusivity or sexual content; no DA re-entry or post-Short 01 career outcome.
Textual Japanese only; no performed voice.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded by the sampled settings and relationships. Not READY: the lethal threshold, risk-consent modifier and post-Short 01 life are open.

conditions: Settings sampled: café work and accounting, shopping, aquarium and outing plans, household chores and janken, festival service, school-work refusal of leisure.
Begin from function or specification, use trusted delegation or comparison, and increasingly state a plain preference; preferences may be practical or profit-shaped.
Operational habit persists in ordinary settings (concealed armament, check-in rules), and she resists context correction while the exchange stays safe.
scenario_readiness.note: Low-stakes behavior is sampled in many settings, mostly with Chisato and the café circle.

conditions: Matched dilemmas only: responsibility for a consequential failure with shared causes, institution against a person-specific rescue, punishment against rescue, mission coordination against an individual's ethic.
Present outcome-centered reasoning and competence-based risk to others as available; do not import Chisato's universal non-killing rule.
No forecast of a lethal threshold outside Chisato-threat or captive cases.
scenario_readiness.note: Her positions are located and reasoned; the weighing in unsampled lethal or consent cases is open.

The relationship ledger repeatedly records that romantic status, exclusivity and sexual intent are not declared and must not be promoted from domestic or yuri-compatible coding. Close partnership, attachment language and physical permissions are covered under relationship conditioning, not as romance.

conditions: Lycoris operations (protection, extraction, rescue, interrogation, precision fire) and café business (accounting, supply, menu, events).
Supported: route briefings, threat identification, self-initiated protection structure, concise coordination, failure reports and apology, procedure redesign.
Not supported: DA command behavior after the exit, careers after Short 01, or unsampled institutions.
scenario_readiness.note: Her best-sampled domains. Not READY: risk-consent and lethal limits are open.

known_limits.statement: Perceptual performed voice is UNVERIFIED in both ledgers; acoustic activation measures state energy, not affect, sincerity or importance, so no delivery label may be drawn from it.

The TV audiovisual corrections table revises the Episode 1 risk records: Erika explicitly asked her teammates to fire, while Saori had no comparable choice, so the lack-of-negotiation modifier applies to the Saori conduct. It also downgrades the claim of certain physical custody of the heart in Episode 12.
Romantic status, exclusivity and sexual intent toward Chisato are not declared through Short 01; domestic and physical permissions must not be promoted to them.
Her real-stakes lethal threshold is open: the norm rests on an abstract answer (TAK-LETHAL-NORM-01), disabling fire on one instance (TAK-FORCE-DISCRIM-01) and coercion of one captive.
Whether closeness or consent modifies her competence-based imposition of risk on others is recorded as open in TAK-OPS-RISK-01.
The Episode 12 survival priority is relationship-specific to Chisato under existential threat, and Chisato's direct restraint stopped it.
Privacy yielding, trap inference and disabling precision each rest on one diagnostic case.
Friends Shorts 02-06, the novels, Recollect and anthologies are not admitted; nothing after Short 01 is known.

The episode deep readings, prospective prediction register and its CP4 test results, V1-to-V2 revision ledger, TV claim matrix and disputes register are not curated on this subject; no validation result is cited.

assessment_scope.source_boundary: The subject's four curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read with its front matter, all status canonical: the V2 Takina character monograph (LYCORIS_RECOIL_TAKINA_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md, 117,723 bytes, recorded complete at the CP5 boundary and re-accepted on 23 November); the Chisato-Takina relationship synthesis (96,068 bytes); the V2 character state and microbehavior ledger (166,335 bytes: TAK rows E01-E13 and Short 01, the per-unit Short 02-06 records, TAK snapshots, TAK candidate policies and the negative-evidence and preference registers, read with its TV corrections table, the 23 November source and audit rechecks, the owner listening return dispositions and the retrospective qualification after all six shorts); and the V2 relationship state ledger (78,825 bytes: REL-CHI-TAK, REL-TAK-DA, REL-TAK-FUK, REL-TAK-ERI, REL-TAK-KUR, REL-TAK-YOS, REL-TAK-SAK and REL-CAFE rows and snapshots, with its retrospective qualifications). Governing evidence is original-Japanese A1: TV E01-E13 and Friends Shorts 01-06, located by cue, timestamp, frame and claim or observation ID. The monograph's and synthesis's novel (A2), Recollect (B1) and anthology (C1) comparisons are retrospective and source-local; they are used only as the documents label them and never as television-anime observations (where a document rules a novel finding SPECIFY or PRESSURE on an anime claim, as for her interiority, it is used as that ruling), and Heroine Archive testimony only as attributed production statements. Perceptual performed voice is UNVERIFIED in both ledgers. The CP5 and V2 behavioral reconstructions, the episode and supplementary deep readings, the claim matrices, the verifier returns, the prospective register and the cross-source crosswalk are not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on them directly. No primary source was inspected. The overall tier is judged within the claim scope stated in the declared-scope known limit.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: TV E01-E13 and Friends Shorts 01-06 at the CP5 and SHORT06 freeze, in located states: E01-E03 DA-return orientation, split inside E03 at the fountain (last 千束さん, C0272) and the train home (first bare 千束 and ええ, C0462-0464), followed by the café game she had refused; E04-E08 preference, household systems and café stewardship (E06 protective cohabitation; E07 a return to DA still offered); E09 reinstatement she had meant to refuse, taken because it may help Chisato live, split at the prognosis and at the parting (いってきます, C0379); E10 inside DA with outside life as fallback; E11 split at the departure (分かってます, C0203), with compliance and disclosure to Kusunoki before it (C0063-0078); E12 DA exit completed and the heart crisis, stopped by Chisato's restraint; E13 negotiated division with Fuki, rescue, search and the beach future. Default state: the post-E13 TV endpoint, with Shorts 01-06 informing comparable ordinary situations without a common calendar and not dated relative to the island operation. Novels, Recollect and anthologies supply no TV state. The boundary limits evidence, not knowledge: her DA upbringing and Kyoto transfer (E01 C0157) belong to her at every state.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The curated items integrate her into one model with a stated organizing change: competence and literal criteria present from E01 are redirected toward chosen people and places, and the question of who gets a say in their use moves from her alone to negotiation (monograph, 'How she changes'). The parts are individuated and conditioned: a rule without a criterion draws a clarifying question and literal compliance (TAK-CLARIFY-01); a cost is vetoed by asking who pays, though she will knowingly spend her own future comfort (Gluttony days 14.645-665); responsibility separates her authorship from others' causal share once she knows it (E03 against E06 C0451-0454); an institution is valued as identity, then used, then left when it cannot save Chisato (E03; E09; E11 C0203); Chisato under existential threat with a concrete lever outranks punishment, status and Chisato's ethic, with Chisato's restraint as the observed stop (E12). The model predicts her overreach and errors: imposed risk, self-blame without the causal facts, the misread parfait and menu, compliance and disclosure to Kusunoki in E11 (C0063-0078), the unchecked rifle chamber she owns (Recovery days 10.559-590). It transfers: the novels place her in situations the anime does not contain and the same dispositions operate (naming the cost or the safe plan, then carrying out Chisato's; OD-12 and OD-20, SPECIFY), and the anthology contributors found the same traits portable. The documents give those sources no predictive credit, so this shows portability, not validation. The two E12 readings, attachment overriding ethics or an ethic of her own, predict the same conduct when Chisato's life is at stake and a lever exists; they diverge for another person's rescue, which is excluded with the risk-consent modifier and her lethal threshold outside person-specific rescue (declared-scope). Not B: within the declared scope no competing motive is left undecided where the model must choose.

The course is integrated and causally explained, and late disclosure of traits present from E01 is kept apart from change (monograph, 'How she changes'). States are located to the cue: DA return as the goal through E03; the lost seat, the fountain, おあいこ, ええ and the first bare 千束 (C0272, C0462); preferences, systems and stewardship in E04-E08 with a return still offered in E07; reinstatement she had meant to refuse, taken for Chisato (E09 C0272-0280); outside life as fallback (E10 C0127-0129); the forfeited return (E11); the E12 crisis; negotiated competence and the future proposal (E13). The shorts test the endpoint in ordinary forms. The shorts and supplementary sources are deliberately left uncalendared rather than forced onto the TV order; that preserved chronology limits placement, not the model. Not B: transitions are explained by what changed, and a state can be selected before predicting.

Her written Japanese is constrained to A level: 私; the address change to Chisato dated to the cue (last 千束さん E03 C0272, first bare 千束 C0462, none later) while です/ます persists; plain forms at located marked moments, crisis and non-crisis (E08 C0421 and C0427; E12; E12 C0454; E13 C0357); あなた at pressure peaks with Chisato and coldly to Majima; お前 to those threatening Chisato (E09 C0012; E12 C0095-0102); ミズキさん, フキさん, once クルミさん, 店長, 司令 and a bare エリカ; institutional words at home (組員, 支給); short dry jabs; a stilted lie (Short 06 C007); a public admission narrower than the private one (Short 02 C041-059). Not A: the governing source is performed, and perceptual delivery is UNVERIFIED in both ledgers; the monograph's author did not audition the uninterrupted performances, and it finds no rule by which her delivery changes with familiarity. That is missing evidence about a channel of the source, recorded here and in DIALOGUE, not a barrier to the overall tier. Not C: forms, recipients and triggers are located across nineteen films.

Ordinary conduct is integrated by function-first reasoning that learns to want: a specification sought, then delegation or comparison, then a plain preference (E04); a costed solution volunteered and revised when its social meaning becomes legible (E08 parfait; Short 03); administrative care (the check-up, the three-ring rule, E08); appetite named without justification (the karintō, E04). Shorts 01-06 sample seasonal service, travel planning, a menu with a held price veto (C077-081), a compensation demand (Short 04) and a room search (Short 05 C027-029). The novels extend the same pattern into settings the anime does not show: the protein shake correct by the stated requirements (Ordinary days 14.19-31), cooking she overestimates and is pleased by (14.308-385), coffee she has learned to understand (Recovery days 9.8-31), cinema objected to on price and time (9.105-112), tastes identified at a sushi bar (Ordinary days 14.111-159). Not B: the habits recur across sources and settings with conditions and revisions.

Each tie is read by direction and stage, and the dyad synthesis compresses initiative, disclosure, withholding, decision, care and teasing on both sides of the central relationship with its change across A1. With Chisato: formal reserve, a condition set on teasing (E04 C0248), bodily verification after a remembered privacy condition (E05), cohabitation ended on her terms (E06), stewardship and the private gift (E08), the planned day (E09), maximum-stakes disagreement without rupture (E12), search, quarrel and future proposal (E13). With DA and Kusunoki: identity, instrument, exit, compliance first in E11. With Fuki: the blow, おあいこ, 行けよ, 私たちで決めましょう. With Erika: thanks and a jab (E12). With Kurumi: no scapegoat, cooperation required (E06). Captives and a subordinate witness meet coercion (E10; Short 05); clients, customers and professional opponents meet different conduct again (monograph). The novels add Mika (his coffee before she can refuse, Recovery days 9.8-31) and Mizuki (the sink slapped at 卑屈, Ordinary days 14.266-271). The name of the bond with Chisato is unsettled in every source; that is an open label, not a gap in the model. Not B: her conduct differs by relationship, stake and stage in located, explained and individuated ways. Abstain on her private view of Fuki, which no source gives.

The anime never narrates her thoughts, but the curated monograph and synthesis bring the creator-proximate novels' close third-person interior to bear on the anime through explicit comparative rulings, and those rulings give a consistent account of what lies behind her stated reasons. Her spoken reasons are often hygienic, commercial or procedural while the narration gives the concern or pleasure behind them (心配はしてません against the narrated care, Recovery days 12.44-46; the enjoyed outing admitted only to herself, 18.26-32; RD-09, SPECIFY). Spoken assent can diverge from a private rule (了解です while already resolved to kill, Gluttony days 10.203-231; GD-06, PRESSURE and SPECIFY). She expects to be of little concern to anyone and is caught out by care (Recovery days 12.664-673, 14.353-358), and she knows where her reading of people falls short (Gluttony days 10.258-269). The anime's own admissions fit that account: 全部 自分のせい (E03); 断ろうと思ってました and 分かりません (E09); outside life rather fun (E10); 嫌だ 千束が死ぬのは嫌だ (E12); and in Short 02 a public half-denial to Kusunoki beside a private 私も 浮かれてますから (C041-059), the gap RD-09 describes, shown in A1 itself. Not A: the monograph says A1 can neither confirm nor refute the novels' private rule, the novel interior is confined to the scenes she focalizes, dream passages stay dream-framed, and her private reasons at particular anime moments (the red uniform, the snow, the E12 tower) remain inferences. Not C: the interior pattern is located in creator-proximate prose, ruled onto the anime claims it bears on, and matched by located A1 admissions.

The supported conflict modes form one pattern: she argues from mechanism, role and consequence (E02), names the cost or proposes the safe plan and then carries out Chisato's (Ordinary days 12.134-148; OD-12, OD-20), refuses a tease that deflects a serious point (E04 C0248), settles a personal score by symbolic reciprocity rather than efficiency (E03), contests to the limit when Chisato's life is at stake and is stopped by Chisato's restraint, yielding once of her own accord (E12 C0153), drops into plain speech in a quarrel she is entitled to (E13 C0357), and resists playful correction without rupture (Short 01). She holds a cost veto against the group (Short 03) and pressures a subordinate witness (Short 05). Lethal escalation outside person-specific rescue is excluded (declared-scope). Not B: within that scope what escalates, limits and ends her conflicts is located and individuated. Response to deliberate betrayal is untested and is an abstention, not a gap in the pattern.

How she deliberates is modeled even where the decision is not: outcome-centred and mechanism-first (最も合理的, E01); team coordination against an individual's ethic (E02); authorship separated from causal share, with a duty of repair (E06); punishment set aside once rescue is reachable (E12); a plural decision with a peer (E13); accountability after an event drawn more finely than consent before one (monograph). The novels show the deliberation continuing privately: a spoken 了解です beside a private resolve to kill (Gluttony days 10.203-231; GD-06), hesitation at a customer-like target (9.827-836), and an intent dulled by Chisato's voice (10.542-570). Those cases show a genuinely conditional disposition, not missing evidence. Not A: the modifier that governs how far another person's consent or closeness limits the risk she imposes is missing from the evidence (TAK-OPS-RISK-01), and it is part of how she weighs others' say. Her lethal threshold outside person-specific rescue stays excluded. Not C: the deliberation is located, reasoned and individuated against Chisato's.

Her humour is integrated and individuated: dry, compressed and often mistaken for literalism, present from the first day (E01 tower; あり過ぎますね, C0306), with conditions for when it appears and when she refuses it. A short jab comes in a safe frame (the E02 bear hacker; the E07 eyesight joke, C0081, and the 蒲焼太郎 alias; 確かに ひどいヤツだ, E12 C0454; これが隠ぺいです turning her own Short 04 word, Short 06 C019). She laughs openly at Chisato's embarrassment (E04) and delights in a game she has analysed and won (E06). A tease that deflects a serious question is refused (E04 C0248; E06 C0206-0209). It transfers: she claims a joke as her own and is told she has started to talk back (Recollect V01 S100-101), labels a joke when she expects it to be missed (Ordinary days 22.2-32) and authors a pun under Chisato's rule (R2-04, EXTEND). Not B: the evidence says when play appears, how she plays, when she refuses it, and that the pattern holds across sources. Delivery is unverified and recorded under VOICE_REGISTER.

Both ledgers cover all nineteen A1 films in original Japanese, with the TV corrections, the 23 November source and audit rechecks and the owner listening return applied. The monograph, recorded COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY and re-accepted with self-containment and fidelity PASS, integrates the three novels, both Recollect volumes, the seven anthologies and the Heroine Archive testimony with an attributed ruling on each. The dyad synthesis covers both directions across the same sources. Derivation from the same ledgers is expected, not a deficiency. Not B: coverage of the governing source and of the admitted supplementary sources is complete. The remaining gap, unverified performed voice, is recorded once under VOICE_REGISTER; the uncurated operational reconstruction is recorded as a known limit.

The negative-evidence register rejects rival models on located opportunities: emotional emptiness (E01; E02), literal-only incapacity for play (E01), instant conversion to café life (E01; E03), invariant flatness, personality replacement (E02; E04; E05), dependency or fusion (E06; E07), moral convergence with Chisato (E07; E08), uncomplicated happiness at reinstatement (E09), DA as total identity (E10; E11), revenge as objective (E12) and unilateral competence (E13). The rechecks corrected attributions (E06 C0318-0320 are Mizuki's; E11 C0430 is Majima's), which strengthens rather than weakens the register. The monograph adds affirmative limits: she cannot perform a lie (Short 06 C007), never says 相棒 aloud in the anime, gives no waking romantic declaration and shows no global conversion in her use of force. Both syntheses list explicit abstentions. Not B: the exclusions are opportunity-sensitive, located and corrected where the source required it.

States are placed to the episode, timestamp and cue: the address change at E03 C0272 and C0462, the E09 prognosis and parting, the E11 departure at C0203, the E12 sequence from 08:07 to 10:36, the first visible discharge on the island at E13 16:07.675; within-episode changes are separated. The shorts and supplementary sources are kept without a common calendar because the sources give none, which is faithful chronology rather than imprecision. Not B: any TV state can be selected before predicting, and the unplaced material is marked as such.

conditions: Output is illustrative written Japanese, never quotation; no pitch, warmth, deadpan or other performed delivery is claimed, because perceptual voice is UNVERIFIED.
Choose the state and the listener first. To Chisato: 千束さん through E03 C0272 and bare 千束 from C0462; です/ます stays her default after the name change.

Plain forms occur at located marked moments, not only in crisis: the E08 gift and café (でしょ), the E12 tower (嫌だ 千束が死ぬのは嫌だ), the E12 jab to Erika (確かに ひどいヤツだ) and the E13 forest quarrel (アホは そっちでしょ). Do not make plain speech her default with Chisato; wider transfer of these forms is open.
お前 only to a person threatening Chisato; あなた at pressure peaks with Chisato and coldly to Majima; さん for Mizuki and Fuki; 店長 for Mika; 司令 for Kusunoki; a bare エリカ.

Jabs are short, dry and literal; a tease that deflects a serious point is refused; an attempted lie comes out stilted and she falls back on the literal truth (Short 06); a public admission may be narrower than the private one (Short 02).

Listeners sampled in the anime: Chisato, Fuki, Erika, Kurumi, Mizuki, Mika, Kusunoki, Sakura, Yoshimatsu, Majima, Himegama, a client, a captive and fans. Another listener is a separate, lower-confidence condition limited to these register rules. Novel and comic lines are not anime speech, and dream lines are not waking speech.
scenario_readiness.note: The address inventory, the dated name change and the located plain forms constrain illustrative Japanese closely enough for bounded use. Not READY: delivery is unverified, and the monograph finds no rule by which her voice changes with familiarity. Not NOT_READY: forms and triggers are located across the TV episodes and shorts.

conditions: Select a located state first. The default is the post-E13 TV endpoint, with Shorts 01-06 informing comparable ordinary situations without being dated relative to the island operation.
A rule, assignment or norm without a stated criterion: predict a clarifying question, then literal compliance with the criterion once it is supplied.

A new protection or rescue problem: predict self-initiated structure, concise coordination and precise fire; at the endpoint she negotiates the division with a competent peer (E13) rather than authorizing herself. Include her overreach: risk imposed on another on the strength of her competence, without that person's say (Saori, E01).

Chisato under a credible existential threat with a concrete rescue option: predict that Chisato's survival outranks punishment, status and Chisato's stated ethic, and that force escalates only as far as that option requires; the observed stop is Chisato's own restraint and refusal (E12). Both gates are required. The two readings of E12 agree here; they diverge for another person's rescue, which is not predicted, and her lethal threshold outside person-specific rescue is excluded.

A loss she had a hand in: she claims her own choice, separates others' causal share once she knows it and asks for repair rather than blame; while causes are hidden she over-attributes to herself (E03).
An ordinary task with an intelligible goal: a costed solution volunteered, possibly a product of her own; she may misread how others will see it, then withdraws it or holds a cost veto.
An institutional offer against Chisato's rescue: she uses the institution while it helps and leaves when it cannot (E09-E11); under pressure her first move can still be compliance (E11 C0078).

In an unfamiliar ethical situation inside the scope, model how she deliberates (mechanism, cost, who pays, authorship and causal share, the safe plan named before deferring to a partner's) without asserting a unique decision where the evidence shows a conditional disposition.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One located TV state: E01-E03 DA-return orientation, split inside E03 at the fountain and the train (C0272; C0462); E04-E08 café learning and stewardship (E06 cohabitation; E07 return still offered); E09 reinstatement taken for Chisato, before or after the parting; E10 inside DA; E11 before or after the departure (C0203); the E12 crisis; or the post-E13 endpoint, the default, with the shorts as comparable ordinary situations without a calendar. Her knowledge follows the TV order (the heart from E05, Kurumi's part in the hack from E06, the prognosis from E09). Her DA upbringing and Kyoto transfer belong to her at every state; what she is never shown learning (the inscribed farewell card, how Mika obtained the heart, the call Chisato keeps from her in the epilogue) stays unknown to her.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Chisato as partner; Fuki, Erika, Kurumi, Mizuki, Mika and Kusunoki as located relations; Yoshimatsu, Majima and Himegama as threats to Chisato; a client, a captive, a subordinate witness and fans as sampled stranger roles, each receiving different conduct. Another close relationship, an unfamiliar admirer or a stranger whose needs are unclear is a separate, lower-confidence transfer, and conduct toward a captive does not transfer to a customer.
setting_constraints: Café work and accounts, the household, outings, protection, rescue and DA operations, matched in stakes to the located cases.
No romance declaration, exclusivity or sexual content; no adoption of Chisato's nonkilling rule; no 相棒 said aloud by Takina; no permanent shared residence; no DA re-entry or career after the shorts.
No novel, comic or dream content imported as anime behavior or waking speech; no performed voice.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded extrapolation from an integrated, individuated model whose dispositions recur across sources. Not READY: the risk-consent modifier and her lethal threshold outside person-specific rescue are excluded, the two E12 readings diverge for another person's rescue, and delivery is unverified. Not NOT_READY: the conditions that change her choices are located and stated.

conditions: Settings sampled: café service, accounts and menu, shopping, the aquarium, the household and janken, school work, the scheduled outing, seasonal service, travel planning, a ghost-hunt prank and visitors to the café (E02-E09; Shorts 01-06).
Predict function or specification first, trusted delegation or comparison, an increasingly plain stated preference, a costed proposal, and care shown more in act than in word.
Operational habit persists in ordinary settings (the concealed handgun; the check-in rule), and she resists correction while the exchange stays safe.
Her private life outside the café circle, and tastes shown only in the novels and comics, are not established for this continuity and are not filled in.
scenario_readiness.note: Not READY: ordinary conduct is sampled mostly with Chisato and the café circle, and the shorts test work and leisure rather than crisis-level care. Not NOT_READY: low-stakes behavior is located across many scenes.

conditions: Matched dilemmas only: responsibility for a failure with shared causes; an institution against a person-specific rescue; punishment against rescue; mission coordination against a partner's ethic.

Predict outcome-centred reasoning, competence-based risk to others as available, and her distinction between her own authorship and others' causal share; do not import Chisato's universal nonkilling rule.

Model her deliberation rather than assert a unique outcome where her disposition is conditional; abstain on her lethal threshold outside person-specific rescue and on how consent or closeness limits the risk she imposes.
scenario_readiness.note: Not READY: the deciding consideration in unsampled lethal or consent cases is not established. Not NOT_READY: her positions are located, reasoned and distinct from Chisato's.

The evidence bounds this scenario affirmatively rather than falling silent. The monograph and the dyad synthesis find a particular, reciprocated attachment whose name no source settles; the relationship ledger records romantic status, exclusivity and sexual intent as undeclared through Short 06; the closest novel scenes are dream-framed, her one waking word for the bond to a stranger is 友人 while Chisato's is 相棒, and in the anime she refuses a tease about boys (E06 C0206-0209). The synthesis says to abstain from predicting a romantic declaration or an exclusive arrangement, and the monograph finds no warranted romantic script for an unfamiliar admirer. Close partnership, physical permissions and attachment language are assessed under relationship conditioning, not as romance.

conditions: Lycoris operations: route briefings, threat identification, self-initiated protection, concise coordination, precision fire, failure reports and apology, and severe, bounded coercion of a captive (E10).

Conflict with a direct order has two located cases: E01, where she overrides an order to wait in order to save Erika and defends it as 最も合理的, and E11, where after reinstatement she first complies and then forfeits her return to rescue Chisato. Other order conflicts are not predicted.
Café business: accounts, supply, menu, events, receipts and a price veto; she may misread how a product she designs will be seen.
Not supported: DA command roles after the exit, careers after the shorts, or unsampled institutions.
scenario_readiness.note: Her best-sampled domains. Not READY: the risk-consent modifier and her lethal limits are open. Not NOT_READY: conduct in both domains is located with counterconditions.

known_limits.statement: The overall tier A is judged within a declared claim scope: ordinary life, café and Lycoris professional conduct, interpersonal relationships, humour and play, practical reasoning, and the supported portions of conflict and ethical behavior, including the two-gate rescue of Chisato. Excluded, and not predicted: her lethal threshold outside person-specific rescue contexts; the modifier by which another person's consent or closeness limits the risk she imposes; the rescue of a person other than Chisato under existential threat; romance; and anything after the shorts. Outside the scope the evidence supports abstention, not a lower-tier prediction.

Perceptual performed voice is UNVERIFIED in both ledgers, and the monograph's author did not audition the uninterrupted Japanese performances. Acoustic activation measures state energy, not affect or importance, and the owner listening return settles particular speaker attributions, not delivery.

The anime never narrates her thoughts. The novels' interior reaches this continuity only through the curated documents' SPECIFY and PRESSURE rulings (RD-09; GD-06), and A1 can neither confirm nor refute it; her private reasons at particular anime moments remain inferences.

The novel, Recollect and anthology findings are retrospective and source-local: they can specify, extend or pressure a TV reading but never rewrite it, and dream content stays dream-framed. The v2-monograph-tv coverage item claims none of them as television-anime coverage.

Whether consent or closeness modifies her competence-based imposition of risk on others is open (TAK-OPS-RISK-01); the TV correction applies the lack-of-negotiation modifier to Saori, not to Erika, who asked her teammates to fire.

Her lethal readiness is shown under threat to Chisato, against attackers and with a captive. The norm rests partly on an abstract answer (TAK-LETHAL-NORM-01), and the monograph says her threshold for Chisato does not transfer to a stranger whose needs are unclear.

Her E12 conduct can be read as attachment overriding ethics or as an ethic of her own in which one particular life outweighs a doctrine; the films let both stand. Both predict the same conduct when Chisato's life is at stake and a concrete lever exists; they diverge for the rescue of another person, which is the unsupported transfer condition.
Romantic status, exclusivity and the name of the bond with Chisato are unsettled in every source, and she never says 相棒 aloud in the anime.
The shorts have no common calendar and their link to the TV island operation is open; the ledger records that strong person-specific practical care by Takina remains untested in the six shorts.
Privacy yielding (E07), trap inference (E11) and disabling precision fire (E06) each rest on one diagnostic case.

The monograph's conditional table describes likely conduct; it is not a validated reconstruction and supplies no withheld test result. Under the owner's A/B direction this is recorded as a limit on confidence, not a barrier to the tier.
Her birth family, her life before DA, how she entered DA, why she was transferred from Kyoto and what first tied her worth to usefulness are not shown.

The V2 operational reconstruction (revised after its withheld evaluation and not independently reviewed since, so not on the discovery row), the CP5 behavioral reconstruction, the episode and supplementary deep readings, the claim matrices and verifier returns, the prospective register and the cross-source crosswalk are not curated on this subject, so no validation or probe result is cited.
